world.summary: Built the §3 sea. Map: Tiled source assets/source/maps/slice-sea.tmj (documented subset in packages/content/src/tiledMap.ts) converted by scripts/build-map.ts (npm run map:build / map:check, via tsx) into packages/content/src/maps/sliceSea.ts; validateSeaMap checks four small islands with docks, shoals, eight outer-sea spawn slots pairwise beyond ENGAGEMENT_RANGE_TILES (6), reachability, nearest-island 20-40 s (actual 22-23 s), longest crossing <= 90 s (54 s) and first dock <= 40 s; a unit drift test (Vite ?raw import, content tsconfig unchanged) fails when the module is out of date. Simulation: 64-heading literal cosine table, throttle/brake/slow reverse/drag/turn, swept axis-separated hull collision (slides, runs aground, no tunnelling at any speed), docking with E at low speed near a dock (records dock id, throttle casts off), placeShip, visibleShipIds; state stays integer. Server: ships map tagged .view(), per-client StateView updated after every mirror, public players count, protocol v3, test-only POST /__test/place served only when the dev/test entry (apps/server/src/dev.ts) reads PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_PLACEMENT=1. Web: keyboard helm with E, Phaser tilemap (sea cells left empty for software-renderer speed), camera follow, sight circle, only-visible ships listed and drawn, HUD dock state, minimap with client-side fog. Docs: architecture.md and README updated. Checks I ran: npm run typecheck (pass), npm run test:unit (131 passed), npm run test:integration (21 passed, incl. visibility on decoded state and raw frames), npm run build (pass, smoke also checks the production entry has no placement route), Playwright all four scenarios passed three times; the JSON-report run passed workflow check-report (4 ok).
open_assumptions: The .tmj was laid out with a throwaway script (not in the repo) and never opened in the Tiled editor (not installed); it follows Tiled 1.10+ JSON conventions with an image-less tileset because art is placeholder-only.

Travel targets are read as: each island's nearest other island by sea, dock to dock, 20-40 s; longest useful crossing = longest shortest path between any two docks or spawn slots; §2's first useful stop checked as nearest dock <= 40 s with no lower bound.
'Outer sea' means outside the bounding box of the island rectangles; spawn slots are checked pairwise (stronger than adjacent-only) against ENGAGEMENT_RANGE_TILES = 6; SIGHT_RADIUS_TILES = 10.
Input message fields keep their names (moveX turns, moveY is the throttle, negative ahead); their meaning changed, so PROTOCOL_VERSION is now 3.
Dock labels use the four cardinal sides of the island rectangle (e.g. 'Palm Key, south dock').

Browser tests place ships through the test-only route and steer with a closed-loop keyboard autopilot reading the HUD's authoritative readout; sea scenarios have a 120 s timeout for a loaded verifier.

# Decisions: world-sea

From the operator session of 2026-09-24 (slice planning after the skeleton merged into `main`). These are the recommended defaults; rerun `/workflow-grill world-sea` before launch to revise them.

## Decisions

- Scope is slice 2 of the plan: map, sailing, docking and server-enforced visibility, running in parallel with `duel-core`. On-foot island exploration, ruins, loot and encounters come later.
- One fullstack lane (`world`). A server/web split would fail the worker phase: typecheck gates each lane in isolation, and the web lane would compile against the server lane's new state types.
- The four slice islands follow §18 stage 2 ("four small islands"). The 12-island layout waits for the alpha.
- Map pipeline: Tiled JSON (`.tmj`) source in `assets/source/maps/`, converted by a script into a typed module in `packages/content/src/`, with a drift test. This follows §17 ("author maps in a tile editor and export a documented format") without changing tsconfig files the lane doesn't own.
- Sailing controls: up is throttle, down is brake (and slow reverse from a stop), left and right turn, E docks. These are §8's defaults for movement and interact.
- Visibility is enforced on the server per client (Colyseus `StateView`). Terrain is public static content, so the minimap fog is client-side. Enemy ships are the only hidden state in this slice.
- The existing browser scenarios keep their ids. `two-ships-sync` now means two ships within sight of each other, and the tests may use a test-only placement setting to get there.
- This feature owns the root `package.json`, the lockfile, `README.md` and `docs/architecture.md`; `duel-core` owns none of them, so the two branches don't conflict.

## Assumptions

- The sight radius is a content constant, about 10 tiles, and larger than the engagement range. The engagement range is also a content constant, used here only by the spawn validator.
- The integer heading resolution is the worker's choice (for example 64 or 256 directions) with a literal lookup table. Handling should feel generous rather than simulated (§3).
- `MatchRoom` keeps one room per match, the 1–8 player private matches and the three-layer admission from `skeleton-fixes`.
- The camera follows the player's ship. The map can be larger than the canvas.
- The patch rate stays at 20 Hz. `StateView` filtering must keep the room within its 60 Hz step budget with 8 ships.

## Deferred

- Walking on islands, ruins and rubbings, loot, rumors, fog secrets and the final island: `objectives-endgame`.
- Grapples and challenges (the engagement range as a mechanic): `encounters-theft`.
- The 12-island alpha map, landmarks, slow-zone hazards and sail tonics.
- Art: tilesets and ship sprites replacing the placeholder shapes.

concerns.message: The player count comes from the synced ships map. `hud.ts:25` renders `model.ships.length`, `HeadlessClient.playerCount` returns `state.ships.size`, and `scripts/smoke-build.ts:111` plus the admission and match integration tests wait for `playerCount === 2/4/8`. Once StateView filters ships, that number becomes "ships I can see". The skeleton's spawn slots are about 20 tiles apart and the planned sight radius is about 10 tiles, so each client sees only itself. The plan never says where the true player count comes from.
concerns.consequence: The integration tests that wait for 4 or 8 players time out. Worse, the HUD shows '1' in a two-player match with the ships out of sight, and no browser scenario catches it: join-private-match checks only one player. The quick fixes are either a wrong HUD or a public per-player record that carries slot or position and leaks it. Add a public count-only field (for example `playerCount` on MatchState) and point the HUD, HeadlessClient and smoke build at it.

concerns.message: The drift test cannot live in `packages/content/src`. `tests/unit/purity.test.ts` bans `fs` imports in the pure packages and scans `.test.ts` files too, and the content tsconfig has `types: []`, so there are no Node types. `tests/unit` is not an owned path. The only unit-test location that is both in bounds and in the unit project is `apps/*/src/**/*.test.ts`.
concerns.consequence: A worker who writes `packages/content/src/map.test.ts` with `readFileSync` fails purity and typecheck. They may then report `blocked` under the 'needs a path outside owned paths' stop rule. Tell them up front: put the converter's core in content as a pure function (parsed tmj object → module text), keep a thin fs wrapper in `scripts/`, and put the drift test in e.g. `apps/server/src/seaMap.test.ts`, which reads the .tmj, runs the pure converter and compares against the generated file.

concerns.message: The example placement setting ("an environment variable read by the dev and test entry points") is global to the server process. But `tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts` starts one server for all four scenarios, and they need different layouts: two ships in sight (two-ships-sync), two ships out of sight (out-of-sight), and one ship near a shoal and dock (sail-and-dock). Also, `createMatchOptionsSchema` is a non-strict `z.object`, which silently strips unknown keys, so an extra create option quietly disappears unless the schema is changed.
concerns.consequence: A static spawn list set by an env var can't satisfy all three scenarios, which means rework mid-run. The likely workarounds are hacks such as starting two ships in sight and sailing one away. Better: the env var only unlocks a per-match placement request, such as a gated debug message or an optional layout field that the server ignores unless the flag is set. It never touches admission, and it gets its own test showing it is inert by default.

concerns.message: The travel-time targets set the map's scale, and the plan leaves that open. At the skeleton's 5 tiles/s, neighbouring islands 20–40 s apart means 100–200 tiles of sea between them, so the map is roughly 250×250 tiles, or more than 60k cells. A map that size can't realistically be hand-authored as a .tmj, becomes a huge literal module, and gets drawn tile by tile in Phaser.
concerns.consequence: If max speed and tile scale are not fixed first, the worker gets pushed around by the validator: they re-tune the map, the speed or both several times, the generated module bloats typecheck (keep it as annotated string rows, never a huge `as const` tuple), and drawing one Graphics rect per tile makes the browser tests slow or flaky. Set max speed at about 2–3 tiles/s so the map stays near 100×80 tiles, and draw the terrain once into a texture.

concerns.message: The acceptance does not define "neighbouring islands", "longest useful crossing" or the path metric. The metric has to be integer: octile costs such as 5/7, because `Math.sqrt` is banned in content.
concerns.consequence: The validator can be written to pass vacuously, for example by picking the nearest pair only or measuring island centres instead of docks, and it would still 'fail on a broken map' in some trivial sense. Define it: dock-to-dock shortest sea paths at the content max-speed constant that the simulation also uses; each island's nearest other island is 20–40 s away; the maximum over all dock pairs and spawn-to-nearest-dock is ≤ 90 s; include negative tests (a moved island, a sealed dock).

concerns.message: Driving a ship with acceleration and turning from the keyboard in Playwright is timing-sensitive if the test is open-loop ("hold ArrowUp 1200 ms, ArrowLeft 300 ms"). The server steps at 20 Hz, held input expires after 250 ms, and the test fails when CI speed differs.
concerns.consequence: sail-and-dock and out-of-sight fail intermittently, and a single flaky run fails the browser check (retries: 0). Place the ship next to the shoal and dock with a known heading, and steer in a closed loop: each HUD entry exposes x, y, heading, speed and dock as data attributes, and the test waits on those authoritative values instead of wall-clock sleeps.

concerns.message: duel-core builds on the existing simulation modules (`hash.ts` `hashState`/`canonicalize`, `fixed.ts`, `random.ts`). This lane owns all of `packages/simulation/src` apart from `duel/` and may refactor them. `ShipSchema.heading` is also `t.uint8()`, so any heading resolution above 256 wraps silently.
concerns.consequence: Git merges the two branches cleanly, but the merged tree fails typecheck or the duel determinism tests if an export of these modules is renamed or its signature changes. Only add to fixed.ts, hash.ts and random.ts, never rename or change them. Keep headings at 256 or fewer, or widen the schema field.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Keep what decisions.md settles (Tiled source, one lane, StateView) and cut the moving parts around it. Size the world by lowering max ship speed (about 2–3 tiles/s) so the map stays near 100×80 tiles and can be read and authored as CSV. Keep the existing input shape: moveY for throttle/brake, moveX for turn, one `buttons` bit for interact. That leaves only the version number and a bit constant to change in the protocol. Put a public `playerCount` in MatchState and filter only the ships map. Make the test placement a per-match request that the env var unlocks, not a global spawn list. Put the converter core in content as a pure function with a thin fs wrapper in scripts/, and put the drift test under apps/server/src.
challenge.cheap_experiment: Before any map or sailing work, run a spike of about 30 minutes on the current skeleton. Tag the `ships` field as view-only in `apps/server/src/schema.ts` using @colyseus/schema 5.0.34's `schema()` builder (whatever its `.view()` or `view: true` equivalent is). In `onJoin`, set `client.view = new StateView()` and `view.add` only the client's own ShipSchema. Then write a two-HeadlessClient integration test that checks `b.room.state.ships.get(a.sessionId) === undefined`, calls `view.add(aShip)` on b's view and waits for it to decode, then calls `view.remove` and waits for it to vanish. Also check that `code`, `frame` and a new `playerCount` still arrive. This either confirms the filtering works with the builder API and reflection decoding, or triggers the task's Colyseus stop condition early, before hours of map and sailing work.

# Task: world

## Goal

Turn the skeleton's empty rectangle into the §3 sea: an authored tile map with four small islands, shoals and docks, ships that sail with acceleration, braking and turning and cannot cross land or shoals, docking at island docks, and a sight radius that the server enforces, so no client receives ships it cannot see (§16). Browsers show the map, their own view of nearby ships and a fogged minimap.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §3 (sea and islands: movement, visibility, travel-time targets), §2 ("Spawn fairness"), §16 ("Hidden information") and §17 ("Content definitions": tile-editor maps, validators). Read `docs/architecture.md` and the skeleton code it maps, especially `packages/simulation` (integer state, `step`, `hashState`), `packages/content/src/sea.ts`, `apps/server/src/MatchRoom.ts` and `schema.ts`, and `apps/web`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` (ending with `scripts/smoke-build.ts`) and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`. Playwright's Chromium for `@playwright/test` 1.63.0 is installed and shared read-only; never run `playwright install`.
- Another feature (`duel-core`) runs at the same time and adds `packages/simulation/src/duel`, `packages/content/src/moves`, `packages/test-tools/src/replay` and subpath exports in those three packages' `package.json`. Never create or edit those paths or those three `package.json` files, so the two branches merge cleanly.

## Constraints

- Keep the skeleton's rules: integer fixed-point simulation with no floating-point transcendental functions in the pure packages (an integer heading table written as literal data or generated by a script is fine), the server as the only writer, zod-validated protocol messages, and the private-match admission layers. Change the protocol version, since input changes.
- Use existing tooling: Colyseus `StateView` (or its 0.18 equivalent) for per-client visibility, Phaser for drawing, zod for data validation.
- The map is authored as a Tiled JSON map (`.tmj`, a documented subset) under `assets/source/maps/`. A script under `scripts/` converts it into a typed TypeScript module in `packages/content/src/`. The content package's tsconfig stays unchanged, so do not import JSON directly. A unit test fails when the generated module is out of date with the source map.
- Placeholder art only: coloured tiles and shapes drawn by Phaser, no image files.
- Out of scope: walking on islands, ruins, rubbings, loot, rumors, encounters, fruit, economy, match phases.

## Acceptance

- Map content, validated by unit tests that fail on a broken map:
  - four small islands, each with at least one dock; shoals as obstacles; eight spawn slots on the outer sea;
  - every dock and spawn slot reachable by sea;
  - at full speed on the shortest sea path, neighbouring islands 20–40 s apart and the longest useful crossing at most 90 s;
  - adjacent spawn slots out of engagement range (a named content constant).
- Sailing, unit-tested in `packages/simulation`: throttle forward accelerates to a maximum speed, braking decelerates, turning changes an integer heading at a turn rate, and a ship never enters a land or shoal tile. A collision stops or slides the ship without tunnelling, including at full speed. Docking works with interact near a dock at low speed: it stops the ship and records the dock; any throttle undocks. The whole state stays integer, and the determinism test still holds.
- Visibility, proven on real clients: an integration test with headless clients shows that a ship outside the sight radius is absent from the other client's decoded state, appears when it sails within the radius and disappears when it leaves. A player's own ship is always visible, and terrain needs no sync because the map is static content.
- Browser: the web client draws the tile map, follows the player's ship with the camera, lists and draws only visible ships, shows the docked state in the HUD, and has a minimap whose fog clears around the player's path (client-side is fine, as terrain is public). The four browser scenarios in `policy.json` pass: `join-private-match`, `two-ships-sync`, `sail-and-dock`, `out-of-sight`.
- Tests may place ships deterministically through a test-only server setting, for example an environment variable read only by the dev and test entry points. It is off by default and documented, and it never weakens admission or visibility.
- `docs/architecture.md` describes the map format and pipeline, sailing, docking and the visibility boundary, still within about a page and a half. `README.md` mentions the map script.
- `npm ci` then each of the five policy checks passes from a clean checkout.

Browser checks: each scenario id appears in exactly one test title as `[scenario:<id>]`. That test, when it passes, attaches exactly one image/png named `screenshot:<id>` (other attachments are fine). The verifier refuses anything else. Before completing, run the spec files you changed with a JSON report:

```bash
WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=worker PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE=<tmp>/report.json \
  npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts --reporter=json <spec files>
```

Then check the report with the verifier's own rules: run the exact `check-report` command the controller appends to this task when it pins it.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).
- Colyseus 0.18 offers no per-client state filtering that keeps other ships out of a client's payload.
- A check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths.
- After two and a half hours of work, any required check still fails and you cannot name the next fix.

Report `question` only for a choice that would change this acceptance.

# Decisions: world-sea

From the operator session of 2026-09-24 (slice planning after the skeleton merged into `main`). These are the recommended defaults; rerun `/workflow-grill world-sea` before launch to revise them.

## Decisions

- Scope is slice 2 of the plan: map, sailing, docking and server-enforced visibility, running in parallel with `duel-core`. On-foot island exploration, ruins, loot and encounters come later.
- One fullstack lane (`world`). A server/web split would fail the worker phase: typecheck gates each lane in isolation, and the web lane would compile against the server lane's new state types.
- The four slice islands follow §18 stage 2 ("four small islands"). The 12-island layout waits for the alpha.
- Map pipeline: Tiled JSON (`.tmj`) source in `assets/source/maps/`, converted by a script into a typed module in `packages/content/src/`, with a drift test. This follows §17 ("author maps in a tile editor and export a documented format") without changing tsconfig files the lane doesn't own.
- Sailing controls: up is throttle, down is brake (and slow reverse from a stop), left and right turn, E docks. These are §8's defaults for movement and interact.
- Visibility is enforced on the server per client (Colyseus `StateView`). Terrain is public static content, so the minimap fog is client-side. Enemy ships are the only hidden state in this slice.
- The existing browser scenarios keep their ids. `two-ships-sync` now means two ships within sight of each other, and the tests may use a test-only placement setting to get there.
- This feature owns the root `package.json`, the lockfile, `README.md` and `docs/architecture.md`; `duel-core` owns none of them, so the two branches don't conflict.

## Assumptions

- The sight radius is a content constant, about 10 tiles, and larger than the engagement range. The engagement range is also a content constant, used here only by the spawn validator.
- The integer heading resolution is the worker's choice (for example 64 or 256 directions) with a literal lookup table. Handling should feel generous rather than simulated (§3).
- `MatchRoom` keeps one room per match, the 1–8 player private matches and the three-layer admission from `skeleton-fixes`.
- The camera follows the player's ship. The map can be larger than the canvas.
- The patch rate stays at 20 Hz. `StateView` filtering must keep the room within its 60 Hz step budget with 8 ships.

## Deferred

- Walking on islands, ruins and rubbings, loot, rumors, fog secrets and the final island: `objectives-endgame`.
- Grapples and challenges (the engagement range as a mechanic): `encounters-theft`.
- The 12-island alpha map, landmarks, slow-zone hazards and sail tonics.
- Art: tilesets and ship sprites replacing the placeholder shapes.
